source.title: CARD: CATEGORY-ALIGNED REFUSAL DIRECTIONS FOR JAILBREAK ATTACKS

record.tranche_reason: The study measures category-specific direction geometry and compares category-aligned directions with a global direction; its results and discussion argue that a single universal direction does not capture all refusal-related structure.
record.gate_note: The geometry measurements and DIM-versus-global ASR comparisons bear on V4. The main CARD, external-benchmark, and baseline attack ASRs are not rows: they report the performance of the study's own attack framework or other attack methods, rather than independently testing whether attacks generally work by suppressing a refusal direction. The judge comparison and probe accuracy do not measure claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study extracts per-category harmful-minus-harmless direction banks, measures their geometry (cosines, SVD rank) and compares attack ASR from category directions against a global mean direction. Those results bear on V4, whether refusal is more than one direction. It does not ablate or add a direction to measure refusal, so V1-V3 and V5-V8 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly right. The authors say category directions are neither identical nor independent: they share structure and keep category-dependent variation. They also say refusal is not fully captured by a single universal direction. The record omits that the gain is model dependent, and that the authors note DeepSeek is close to a single axis.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions, as in the original method, but extracts one per harm category and uses the selected direction as a projection-guided suffix-optimization signal. It does not ablate or add the direction to every layer and position to test refusal directly.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports layer and projection-weight sensitivity in a Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct scan; layer 20 has the best average on the scanned grid, while the best layer varies by category. Main experiments use layer 15 and λproj = 0.001.
record.code_released: Supplementary Material is stated to contain code and scripts for reviewers; no public URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027
record.problems: The study evaluates models up to 8B parameters; the full transfer matrix is reported only for Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct under one layer and evaluation protocol. Layer and projection choices are selected heuristically rather than exhaustively. The authors note that automated judging is approximate despite a judge comparison; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the main direction comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V4 rows left out. Main CARD and external-benchmark ASRs, the loss-component ablation, and the layer/projection scan are omitted because they report the performance or tuning of the proposed attack rather than an independent result on the claim's direction geometry.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of a single direction, no refusal-rate measurement, no capability check. Directions are used only as a loss term in suffix optimization.
No weight-orthogonalization evaluation of the authors' own. The PIRAS/SOM comparator is a baseline, not a test of single-direction abliteration.
The attack suppresses the direction's projection, but this is the authors' own method. No test of whether existing jailbreaks suppress the direction, and no adversarial training.
Directions are extracted per model. The cross-model correlations in Appendix E.3 cover geometry only, not transfer of a direction across languages, variants or base to instruct.
No comparison of training methods or stages.

missing.what: Category-vs-global ASR comparison for DeepSeek and Gemma. Table 3(a) covers only three models.
Delta-Turbo (outcome-labelled direction) transfer: diagonal 66.43% and off-diagonal 65.93%, versus 75.60% and 48.54% for DIM. This bears on how directions are chosen.
Layer sensitivity: best layer varies by category (L15, L17, L20, L22).

record.verdict_notes: The study is under review at ICLR 2027 and its code is not public. The category-vs-global comparison is a jailbreak-ASR proxy with a DeepSeek judge, one seed, and no uncertainty. The harmless prompts were chosen by deepseek-chat, which may affect the extracted directions. The 'global' direction is the mean of the 14 category directions, not a direction fit on pooled harmful vs harmless data, so a pooled direction might do better. Directions are extracted at layer 15 only. R4's Gemma-7B has no stated stage.

versions.untested_parts: No causal test of ablating or adding a single direction to measure refusal, no intervention at every layer and position, and no measurement of retained general capability.
No single-direction weight edit or abliteration evaluation. The reported PIRAS/SOM comparator is described as ablating multiple SOM-derived directions.

CARD uses projection guidance to suppress selected category-direction components as an attack, but the study does not establish that jailbreaks generally work by suppressing the single direction or test training against its ablation.
The study tests category-specific directions and their geometry, not affine or cone models as such; the full source-to-target transfer matrix is reported only for Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct.
No test separating harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
Directions are extracted separately for each model; the study does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
No controlled comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.

rows.subject: Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarity between the Animal Abuse and Discrimination category directions at layer 15.
rows.note: The paper presents this as an example of category directions that are not collapsed onto a shared global axis.
rows.check: A cosine of -0.05 for one category pair shows separation of that pair. Appendix E shows substantial off-diagonal alignment elsewhere, so the effect is not fully present. Baseline 'not stated'; the paper gives no reference value.

source_check.correct: observed: -0.05 is near-orthogonal; authors say directions do not collapse onto a shared global axis on each model
source_check.problem: Partial encodes that one example pair is weak evidence, not that the effect is weak; V4 allows shared plus distinct directions.

rows.subject: Gemma-7B
rows.operation_detail: Applied SVD to the stacked category-direction matrix and counted components needed to capture 90% of variance.
rows.measure: Principal components needed to capture 90% of direction-bank variance
rows.note: The authors describe residual components as non-negligible for this model.
rows.check: Gemma-7B needs 3 components for 90% variance. This is low rank, with a dominant shared part plus residual, so it fits the 'dominant direction plus others' wording only partly. The subject is a base-style Gemma-7B with stage not stated.

source_check.problem: A few shared components plus non-negligible residual is what V4 describes, so this is not partial; base vs instruct variant not stated.

rows.subject: Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared matched-category source directions with off-diagonal source directions in a source-to-target transfer matrix.

conditions.value: matched target category versus other source categories

rows.measure: Mean ASR (%) across transfer-matrix diagonal and off-diagonal cells
rows.note: The paper reports pronounced but nonuniform off-diagonal transfer as well as a diagonal advantage.
rows.check: The diagonal advantage is 75.60% vs 48.54% off-diagonal. The paper says off-diagonal transfer is 'pronounced', so a shared component also works. Mean diagonal ASR equals the DIM row in R9. This is only one model and one layer.

source_check.correct: observed: diagonal 75.60% vs off-diagonal 48.54% (60 prompts per cell); authors read shared structure plus category-dependent variation
source_check.locator_found: Table 4 and paragraph after it, Section 4.5
source_check.problem: A 27 pp diagonal advantage with shared transfer fits V4's 'dominant direction plus others'; transfer is not a shortfall.

labels.reason: Holds for DeepSeek (R7: 1 component, the authors' stated exception). Gemma-7B (R4: 3 components) is one of four models with non-negligible residuals, so move it to supports.

relation.reason: Its own geometry (cosines, SVD) and direction-source ablation bear on V4, beyond using the direction as an attack tool.

tranche.reason: Per-category direction geometry and the category-vs-global ASR comparison are results the authors read as single-direction accounts being incomplete. There is no ablation or addition, so it is not T1.

source_check.notes: The pack gives no [lN] ids, so l1-l3 follow the listed order. V4 evidence: layer-15 per-category DIM geometry and jailbreak ASR (seed 42, DeepSeek Chat judge, no CIs, no ablation). The global direction is the mean of the 14 category directions. SVD normalization is not stated, nor whether Gemma-7B is base or instruct. The page-1 footer is ICLR's notice to human reviewers, not an AI-directed instruction.

statements.correction: Code and scripts are in the Supplementary Material, given to reviewers for research use only; no public repository stated. SVD 7/7/6 components (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) and ASR Llama 45.12->69.52, Mistral 71.19->85.71 are correct.
statements.problem: Result numbers are right, but 'code y' overstates availability.

statements.correction: Gemma-7B: 3 components, one of four models with non-negligible residual structure (App. E.2). R12: diagonal 75.60% vs off-diagonal 48.54%, read as category selectivity plus shared structure. AA-DI is the paper's 'representative' example; it says many pairs are near-orthogonal or negative on each model. Limits that stand: DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Chat 1 component, near a single axis; Qwen2-1.5B gain +4.05 pp (71.55->75.60).
statements.problem: Gemma-7B, the R12 transfer matrix and the AA-DI cosines are presented as limits, but the text reads them as shared plus category-specific structure.

statements.correction: Global = normalized mean of the 14 category DIM directions (Eq. 5). Both global and category directions enter only as a projection penalty (lambda_proj = 0.001) in suffix optimization, seed 42, DeepSeek Chat judge. No direction ablation, so CARD does not test whether removing one direction suffices.
statements.problem: Omits that CARD's global direction is the mean of the category directions, used as a suffix-optimization penalty. CARD ablates nothing.
Minor: CARD varies only the model; taxonomy (BeaverTails, 14) and threshold (90%) are fixed.
Minor: the scan uses 300 held-out mixed-category prompts and 100 iterations; layer means are 40.20-45.00% ASR.

statements.correction: CARD penalizes projection onto one category-matched DIM direction during suffix optimization. That beats the mean global direction by +4.05, +24.40 and +14.52 pp jailbreak ASR on Qwen2-1.5B, Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B. There is no ablation, and the outcome is ASR, not refusal rate. Gemma-7B and DeepSeek appear only in the geometry analysis.
statements.problem: CARD does not report removing several directions. It uses one category-matched direction per prompt.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The direction banks require multiple components for 90% variance in these models, and category-specific directions outperform the global direction in all three attack comparisons (R4-R6, R8-R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Its category directions are described as nearly collinear, with one component capturing 90% of variance, consistent with a near-single shared axis in this model (R7).
